  review-check-noL2.sh (reviewed_hash shape+sentinel, -964 bytes) -> review-check.test.sh 75/75, IDENTICAL to the 75/75 baseline.

The natural home already exists and was edited by this change set. review-check.test.sh Section 2 is a matrix of
exactly these legs -- one three-line jq mutation + error_key assertion per artifact-schema refusal
(missing_key:stopped_by, verdict_invalid_enum, stopped_by_invalid_enum, finding_id_malformed,
severity_invalid_enum, finding_item_invalid:not_object/not_array/missing_evidence). The change set modified that
file (line 65, VALID_ART's reviewed_hash literal) so the existing legs keep passing, and added no new row.

The standard's escape hatch was not used either: the F7 contract contains zero occurrences of "UNPAIRED",
"pairing" or "negative control" apart from the claim that .claude/tests/README.md's pairing-requirement section
was read IN FULL. And UNPAIRED is not the right disposition here -- that hatch is written for PROSE checks
("if the thing you are checking is prose..."); these are executable guards in a shipped script, the category of
which the standard says "Not one executable check failed it".
findings.description: Four of the five refusal guards this change set adds have NO regression coverage, and the project closeout requirement that governs this (.claude/tests/README.md "The pairing requirement", cited as binding from CLAUDE.md, and read IN FULL per the F7 contract) is neither satisfied nor discharged by its own UNPAIRED-with-a-reason escape. Proven by mutation, not argued: each guard was deleted alone from the shipped worktree and the five specs most specific to review-record stayed green (327 assertions, 0 failures, per mutant), while the deleted guard demonstrably restored its defect. The two zero-coverage guards are the fixes for the two defects with the worst measured consequences -- both reproduced at clean HEAD this round -- so they sit one line from silently reverting with every suite still green. That is the exact defect class this P0 task exists to close, reintroduced one layer up at the test surface. Remediation is cheap and the pattern already exists: three-line jq mutation legs in review-check.test.sh Section 2 for reviewed_hash_unusable (shape arm) and the artifact-schema risk_threshold_invalid_enum, and a four-leg pair in review-separation-records.sh (16 assertions, 16s) for artifact_task_id_mismatch and reviewer_identity_invalid_chars -- the latter asserting the SPECIFIC misbehaviour, i.e. that without the guard review-check.sh gate reads open_findings=0 / stopped_by=verdict / independent=true / ok=true over an artifact declaring a CRITICAL finding.

findings.evidence:
codex-detect.sh status resolves reviewer_lane=codex on this machine. codex-review.sh:107 validates the REQUEST
before any Sol call; cmd_validate_request has NO shape check on change_set_hash -- review-check.test.sh's
VALID_REQ still carries "change_set_hash":"h" and the spec asserts it VALID (measured: 75/75 with that literal).
The prompt at codex-review.sh:236 asks Sol to emit "reviewed_hash":"<change-set hash from the request>", and the
FORCED-field jq expression (codex-review.sh ~498-504) sets task_id, iterations, risk_threshold, stop_condition,
reviewer_identity, reviewer_model and reviewer_pin -- but NOT reviewed_hash. So after this change set the
64-lowercase-hex requirement is enforced against a value a language model has to reproduce verbatim, and it is
enforced at validate_candidate (codex-review.sh:351) -- AFTER the paid turn. Recovery is malformed_retry=1
(.claude/review-config) corrective turns whose prompt carries only the error_key ("Validation failed:
reviewed_hash_unusable. Emit ONLY the corrected JSON object...") and not the correct value; on failure the driver
calls fail_no_artifact. Before this change, any string Sol emitted passed. No leg exercises the
bad-reviewed_hash -> corrective-turn path: every reviewed_hash literal in codex-review.sh's spec was changed to
well-formed deadbeef x8 in this same change set.
findings.description:
The fix is placed correctly (validate-artifact is genuinely the one ingest path -- verified: exactly one
REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 record template exists, qa-gate.sh:6832 in cmd_review_record, and codex-review.sh routes
through the same validator). But the new strictness lands on the ONE request-authoritative field the paid driver
does not force, so the optional Codex lane can now spend the operator's money and end in a guaranteed refusal.
Fails closed, so it is not a release blocker: QA falls back to the claude lane, which is qa.md's documented
degradation. Fix is one clause: add .reviewed_hash to codex-review.sh's FORCED jq expression (reviewed_hash IS
request-authoritative by qa.md's own definition -- "the change_set_hash from the request"), and/or shape-check
change_set_hash in cmd_validate_request so the refusal happens before the spend. The latter is exactly the
"refuse at the earliest boundary, not at each consumer" lesson (k6re) the specialist itself cited to justify the
placement decision -- applied one schema over.

findings.evidence:
qa-gate.sh's completion-record usage block documents this exact class in prose: "task/role/each field name/the
digest must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$; model/pin use the WIDER model-id class [A-Za-z0-9._:/\[\]-]$ ... both
REJECTED, never sanitised (the claude-workflow-plugin-bjx class)". The review-record block (qa-gate.sh
~2838-2849) says only "Validates the artifact JSON via review-check.sh (the ONE validator) ... Record writer only
-- no approve/Stop enforcement", and documents none of the five new refusals. Measured counts:
artifact_task_id_mismatch = 2 occurrences in qa-gate.sh, BOTH emitters (6653 review-record, 8040 design-record),
0 in docs/*.md; reviewed_hash_unusable = 1 occurrence, its emitter, 0 in docs/. Neither the 64-lowercase-hex rule
nor the sentinel refusal nor the artifact-schema risk_threshold enum appears in any usage block, docs/HOOKS.md, or
qa.md -- and qa.md section 6p.1 still tells QA to set reviewed_hash from the request's change_set_hash with no
note that a degenerate (empty) change set yields the sentinel and is now refused.
findings.description: The new refusals are undocumented in the one place an operator or agent reads first, while the sibling completion-record block documents exactly this class. Add the artifact-schema contract to the review-record usage block (task_id must match the recorded task; reviewed_hash must be 64 lowercase hex and is refused when it is the SHA-256 empty-content sentinel; risk_threshold must rank in the severity enum; iterations/reviewer_identity/risk_threshold/reviewed_hash are rejected, never sanitised, outside [A-Za-z0-9._+-]), and note in qa.md section 6p.1 that a degenerate/empty change set yields the sentinel and is now refused, with the audited exit being approve --no-review followed by a reason.

findings.evidence:
is_sha256_hex (qa-gate.sh:7420) accepts *[!0-9a-fA-F]* -- case-insensitive -- and gates design-review-record's
--design-hash (qa-gate.sh ~8568) and grilling-record's vendor_hash (~7671). The new reviewed_hash guard
(review-check.sh ~470-493) accepts only [0-9a-f] and refuses uppercase deliberately, with a documented reason.
No live impact: every producer in the repo emits lowercase -- workflow-manifest.sh states "All three are
normalised to bare lowercase 64-hex" (line 179), impact-report.sh uses shasum -a 256 / sha256sum (lines 304-307),
and both live outputs measured this round were lowercase (impact-report.sh --hash-only = b834b65ae7...,
workflow-manifest.sh hash-file review-check.sh = 2b424f1b06...). Recorded so a future editor does not relax or
tighten one side alone.
findings.description: Case-strictness asymmetry between the new reviewed_hash guard (lowercase only) and the pre-existing is_sha256_hex (case-insensitive) that gates design_hash and vendor_hash. No live impact: every producer in the repo emits lowercase. Either align the two classes or leave a cross-reference at both sites so neither is changed alone.
